name: Base Two-Gap Fits vs 21 Personnel
formation: Two-Gap Front vs Under-Center 21 Strong Right

summary.motive: Trade penetration for total gap ownership — let linemen engage and control two gaps each so linebackers can run free over the top to every ball carrier.
summary.keyDefender: RILB scraping over the top — he arrives as the unblocked tackler precisely because the line ate every block
summary.whyItWorks: Engaged linemen guarantee no blocker is ever left unaccounted for, so the ball carrier always runs toward a flowing linebacker rather than a blocked hat.
summary.failureMode: Reach blocks: if a tackle hooks an end off the line, the two-gap chain collapses and the scraper runs into open space.

beats.title: 1. The Two-Gap Geometry
beats.text: Three linemen stand squared between gaps rather than shaded into them — each one is responsible for two gaps and plans to win by engagement, not penetration.

beats.title: 2. Engage and Hold the Point
beats.text: The nose absorbs a full double team while the strong end eats the tight-end clamp — every blocker is accounted for and none are moving backward.

beats.title: 3. Linebackers Run the Ladder
beats.text: With the line holding its blocks, both inside linebackers scrape OVER THE TOP of the engaged bodies instead of fighting through them.

beats.title: 4. Funneled Into the Scrape
beats.text: The setting edge forces the cutback inside exactly where the scraping RILB has arrived — the carrier meets the defense’s cleanest tackler.

relations.tell: All three linemen stand square reading blockers instead of charging gaps — slant fronts explode sideways off this exact patient stance.
